movement_profile.arms_and_hands: haka nounou (short armed), performed close to the body, though Vavaʻu tradition allows wilder and wider arm movements
movement_profile.formation_and_space: tiered rows with front row on the ground, subsequent rows on low and high benches, and back rows standing or on tables
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: tiered levels from ground sitting to standing on benches and tables; no jumps
movement_profile.partnering: not applicable / collaborative group seated formation
movement_profile.posture: seated crosslegged on the ground, usually the right leg over the left, with upper body upright

signature_moves.description: Short-armed symbolic hand and arm gestures performed close to the body during the silent tafua and sung sections.
signature_moves.name: Haka Nounou

movement_profile.tempo_feel: increases feverishly as the performance progresses

music_profile.musical_form: drawn from a limited repertoire of about 10 different tunes
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: continuous beating of the nafa drum
music_profile.sound_description: The music opens with the heavy, resonant booming of iron-drum nafa percussion played with decorated sticks, transitioning into a sparse choral singing style using a limited set of traditional melodies that sound alike to the untrained ear.
music_profile.vocal_style: sung lyrics praising the occasion, performed by the langituʻa singers

basic_steps: Sit crosslegged on the ground with the right leg over the left.
Execute close-armed hand gestures (haka nounou) synchronized with the upper body.
Transition from the silent tafua gestural sequence to the sung portion of the performance.
teaching.formation: Staggered rows ranging from seated on the ground in the front to standing on benches and tables in the back.
teaching.level_notes: Front row reserved for highest status or best dancers; children occupy the ends of rows.
teaching.rhythm: Continuous beating of the nafa drum maintaining the ensemble tempo.
